itinerary.cal: Best July through September once the snow on the approach to Kangaroo Pass has melted. No quota permit; it is a one-day climb from the car, and parties usually sleep at the SR 20 hairpin pullout or a nearby Forest Service campground the night before.
itinerary.totalNote: One long car-to-car day: hike to Kangaroo Pass, drop and traverse to the South Face, climb about 8 pitches of 5.8 R, and rappel the standard north-side line.

days.title: Kangaroo Pass approach and South Face climb
days.objective: Climb the South Face and return to the hairpin
days.note: Mountain Project puts the pass about 1 hour from the hairpin, with the South Face reached 2-4 hours from the car after dropping below the pass and traversing. The route is about 800 ft and 8 pitches with route-finding challenges, mixed rock and runout sections (5.8 R). Most parties descend the standard rappel line on the north side, which Mountain Project describes as 3 single-rope 60 m rappels. Gain is derived from the row's elevations (5,160 ft hairpin to 7,572 ft summit); the hours and miles are estimates.

notes: Only Mountain Project pages were reachable; SummitPost and the Mountaineers returned 403. The Mountain Project area page lists Kangaroo Temple at 7,238 ft, while the row has 7,572 ft. The row says the route has 7 pitches; Mountain Project says 8 pitches and 800 ft, Grade III. Distance and total hours are not documented, so 3.5 mi round trip and 10 hours are estimates built from the 2-4 hour approach time.

itinerary.cal: July through September, once the south-side scree gullies are snow-free. A free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit covers the Ingalls Creek camp with no lottery, and most parties take three days: in over Longs Pass, a summit day, then out.
itinerary.totalNote: A 3-day south-side plan: cross Longs Pass to camp on Ingalls Creek, climb about 4,600 ft of scree and 4-5 pitches of the South Headwall on a long summit day, then climb back over Longs Pass to the car.

days.title: Over Longs Pass to Ingalls Creek
days.objective: Reach the Ingalls Creek camp below Longs Pass
days.note: WTA lists Longs Pass at 2.9 mi and about 2,100 ft from the Esmeralda trailhead. From the pass, drop roughly 1,400 ft to camp on Ingalls Creek; Mountain Project notes good camping there but warns of mice. There is no water between the trailhead and the creek. Gain and loss are derived from the row's elevations, and the miles are a row-based estimate.

days.title: South Headwall to the summit and back
days.objective: Climb the South Headwall and return to camp
days.note: From the Ingalls Creek trail, go up the first major clearing west of Ulrich's Couloir into the West Ridge couloir. Take the right fork near 7,000 ft beneath black slabs to the cirque near 8,700 ft. The 4-5 pitches are mostly 4th and low 5th, with two short 5.7 sections and a ledge belay on every pitch (Mountain Project). Several thousand feet of loose scree make this a long day. The usual south-side descent is the Cascadian Couloir back to the creek; climberkyle describes it as about 4,500 ft from the creek to the summit.

days.title: Back over Longs Pass to the car
days.objective: Regain Longs Pass and hike out
days.note: Climb about 1,450 ft from the creek back to Longs Pass, a dry and often hot climb, then descend the switchbacks to the Esmeralda trailhead.

notes: The row grades the route 5.8. Mountain Project lists 5.8 but says the climbing is never harder than 5.7. Day 2 hours and the per-day miles are estimates: the row's 9.2 km is taken as one way to the summit, so the round trip is about 11.5 mi. The row's 5,009 ft gain covers only the trailhead-to-summit net climb; the round trip is about 8,000 ft because Longs Pass has to be crossed twice.

itinerary.cal: July through September; the Stuart Glacier traverse below Goat Pass holds snow well into summer. A free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit covers a Goat Pass bivy (no Enchantment lottery), and most parties take 2 days, with a third day if they bivy near the summit.
itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day plan from the Esmeralda trailhead: bivy at Goat Pass, then climb the Upper North Ridge with the Great Gendarme and descend the Cascadian Couloir over Longs Pass to the car in one long second day.

days.title: Lake Ingalls and Stuart Pass to Goat Pass
days.note: WTA gives 4.5 mi and 2,500 ft to Lake Ingalls, where camping is prohibited at the lake itself. Go around the west side of the lake toward Stuart Pass, then up to the Goat Pass bivies at about 7,650 ft. Treat Goat Pass as a dry camp late in the season. A fast car-to-car party took 3.6 hours from the trailhead to Goat Pass (Steph Abegg). Gain, loss and miles are estimates from WTA plus the row's elevations.

days.title: Upper North Ridge and Cascadian descent
days.objective: Summit via the Great Gendarme and return to the car
days.note: Traverse east below the Stuart Glacier and climb a loose 4th-class gully edge to the North Ridge notch at about 8,200 ft. Above, the Great Gendarme is the 5.9 crux. Descend the Cascadian Couloir to Ingalls Creek, then climb back over Longs Pass to the Esmeralda trailhead. Slower parties bivy just below the summit and finish on day 3 (alpinedave). Gain and loss are derived from the row's elevations and include regaining Longs Pass.

schedule.label: Leave Goat Pass
schedule.detail: Times are from Steph Abegg's July 2026 car-to-car ascent, which passed Goat Pass at this time.

schedule.label: Base of the North Ridge
schedule.detail: About an hour across the glacier traverse to the notch.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Simul-climb the easier ridge terrain where possible.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: About 6 hours of climbing from the notch.

schedule.label: Back at the trailhead
schedule.detail: About 5.5 hours down the Cascadian Couloir and over Longs Pass.

notes: The row's dist_km of 6.4 (about 4 mi) is too short: WTA puts Lake Ingalls alone at 4.5 mi, so the trailhead to the notch is closer to 7 mi. The row's 2,998 ft gain fits the route itself (about 3,000 ft of climbing per Steph Abegg), not the full trip. Day mileages are estimates. Alpinedave's party took 3 days (bivy near Lake Ingalls, then a bivy just below the summit).

itinerary.cal: June through September, once the gully to Pineapple Pass is snow-free; earlier, carry an ice axe. A free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is required at the Snow Lake trailhead. It is a single day from Alpental.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb from Alpental: Source Lake and talus to Pineapple Pass, about 4 pitches of 5.5 dihedrals on the Southwest Face, and a downclimb and rappel back to the basin.

days.title: Pineapple Pass and the Southwest Face
days.objective: Climb the Southwest Face and return to Alpental
days.note: Take the Snow Lake trail and the Source Lake fork, then cross talus and climb the steep gully toward Pineapple Pass. A 2003 party took about 3 hours from Alpental to Pineapple Pass and about 9 hours round trip, including a 2-hour wait (dbelitz). Break off before the South Face notch and climb the open books and slabs to the summit. Descend back to Pineapple Pass, with rappels down the gully as climberkyle describes, then take the talus back to the basin. Gain is derived from the row's elevations; miles double the row's 4.8 km one-way.

notes: Both sources describe the neighbouring South Face, which shares the approach and descent; the SummitPost page specific to the Southwest Face returned 403. Hours are scaled from the South Face timings.

itinerary.cal: Summer and early fall, once the north side has melted out; carry an ice axe if snow remains on the north side. A free self-issued Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit is required at the Snow Lake trailhead. It is a single day from Alpental.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day scramble from Alpental: approach the basin below The Tooth via Source Lake, drop about 100 ft and traverse northwest onto the class 4 North Ridge, then descend to Pineapple Pass.

days.title: Source Lake basin and the North Ridge
days.objective: Scramble the North Ridge and return to Alpental
days.note: Follow the Snow Lake trail and the Source Lake fork, then the cairned climbers' path into the basin below Bryant, Hemlock and The Tooth. From the basin, drop about 100 ft and traverse northwest to the ridge crest for class 4 scrambling to the summit. Descend by rappels toward Pineapple Pass and the gully, as on the South Face (climberkyle), and walk out over the talus. The Alpental-to-Pineapple Pass leg took a 2003 party about 3 hours (dbelitz). Gain is derived from the 3,100 ft trailhead and 5,604 ft summit, plus the 100 ft drop; miles and hours are estimates.

notes: No opened source describes the North Ridge itself; the WTA trip report and SummitPost returned 403. The plan relies on the shared Alpental and Pineapple Pass approach from the sources plus the row's route description. Gain, high point and distance are null in the row, so they were derived from The Tooth's 5,604 ft summit and the 3,100 ft trailhead.

itinerary.cal: June through September; the wall faces south and is in sun most of the day, so cooler days or a late start for the shade suit it. No permit is needed. It is a one-day climb from the SR 20 pullout near milepost 166.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day roadside alpine outing: about an hour up the Supercave gully to the ledges, 3 pitches of 5.11a below Ellen Pea, then rappels and the gully back to the car.

days.title: Supercave gully and Exorcism of Mark Hanna
days.objective: Climb the route and return to the pullout
days.note: From the milepost 166 pullout, head uphill to the talus and the Supercave gully. Mountain Project gives about 1 hour to the lower ledge and about 1 hour 10 minutes to the upper ledge, with the approach about 0.5 mi and 1,285 ft. The route is 3 pitches of 5.11a more or less directly under Ellen Pea. Steph Abegg reports rappelling Ellen Pea with two ropes takes about an hour back to the base.

notes: No opened source has a description of this route's pitches or descent; the OpenBeta page returned 404. Rappelling Ellen Pea is inferred because the route sits under it. The row's 1,900 ft gain looks high for a 0.5 mi, 1,285 ft approach plus 3 pitches. Hours are an estimate.

itinerary.cal: June through September, picking cool days because the south-facing wall bakes and the P2 crux is temperature-sensitive. No permit is needed. It is a one-day climb from the SR 20 pullout near milepost 166.
itinerary.totalNote: A full one-day free climb: about an hour to the treed ledge, 8 pitches and 1,000 ft of 5.10-5.12 through the Supercave, then two-rope rappels down Ellen Pea or a walk-off to the west.

days.title: Supercave gully and the L&H free route
days.objective: Free the L&H route and return to the pullout
days.note: The approach takes about 1 hour from the milepost 166 pullout up the Supercave gully: 0.5 mi and 1,285 ft (Mountain Project). Start from the same treed ledge as The Tiger. The 8 pitches include a 5.12- dyno on P2 and the 5.12 P4, then a traverse into the largest cave and a finish up the upper pitches of Ellen Pea. Descend by rappelling Ellen Pea with two ropes (about an hour to the base per Steph Abegg) or walk off to the west.

notes: Mountain Project lists the route as 1,000 ft, 8 pitches, Grade III, and says the grades are somewhat theoretical. Hours are an estimate; no source gives a total time for the route.

itinerary.cal: June through September. The west face gets afternoon sun, so many parties start mid-morning. Only a Northwest Forest Pass to park is needed. It is a one-day climb from the Blue Lake trailhead.
itinerary.totalNote: A single day from the Blue Lake trailhead: about an hour's approach, roughly 4-5 hours for the 6 pitches of 5.11a, and bolted or original rappels back to the packs.

days.title: Blue Lake approach and NEWS West Face
days.objective: Climb the West Face and return to the trailhead
days.note: Leave the Blue Lake trail at about 1.5 mi and take the climbers' path into the basin; Steph Abegg reports a little over an hour from the car and North Cascades Mountain Guides say about 1.5 hours. The crux is P4, a thin 5.11- tips crack followed by 5.10 fingers. Descend the six-station bolted rappel line about 15 ft right of the finish with a 70 m rope, or take the original rappels via the notch and chockstone; either takes about 40 minutes back to the packs. Gain is derived from the row's elevations; miles are an estimate.

schedule.label: Leave the Blue Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Derived from a 1-hour-plus approach before an 8:55 start.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Shared start with the Northwest Corner (Steph Abegg, 2013).

notes: climbcanada gives about 700 ft of gain to the trail turnoff and about 1,000 ft more to the base, which is consistent with the row's 2,400 ft. The 4.0 mi round trip is an estimate. Steph Abegg's 2006 ascent climbed from about 11:15 AM to 4 PM.

itinerary.cal: July through September, once the Concord-Lexington gully is free of snow. Only a Northwest Forest Pass to park is needed. It is a single day from the Blue Lake trailhead; the route faces southwest and is sunny.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb from the Blue Lake trailhead: a short approach to Concord Tower's west face, 6 pitches and 700 ft of 5.11 with the crux on the first pitch, and two rappels to the Concord-Lexington notch with a gully walk-off.

days.title: Blue Lake approach and Up in Arms
days.objective: Climb Up in Arms and return to the trailhead
days.note: Take the Blue Lake trail to the climbers' trail toward the Liberty-Concord gully, then hug the west wall of Concord to the start, left of the South Face routes. The AAJ calls it perhaps the closest route to the Blue Lake trailhead. The first pitch is the 5.11 crux. Descend with two rappels to the Concord-Lexington notch; Steph Abegg reports they take about 10 minutes. Then walk down the gully, about 1 hour to the climbers' trail and 30-45 minutes more on the Blue Lake trail. Gain is derived from the row's elevations; miles and hours are estimates.

notes: The row has two high points: 7,569 ft and a 7,611 ft summit waypoint. Steph Abegg lists Concord Tower at 7,560 ft. The descent timings come from Steph Abegg's Concord Tower North Face and Liberty Bell Beckey Route reports, which share the notch and gully. Hours and miles are estimates.

itinerary.cal: June through September, once the Squire Creek ford is low enough to cross; it is hard in early season and after storms. No permit is needed. It is a long single day from the car, and some parties camp at Squire Creek Park the night before.
itinerary.totalNote: A long one-day outing: ford Squire Creek and climb the steep forest gullies to the grassy saddle, scramble west past Skeena26 to the far western wall, climb about 5 pitches of 5.8, and return the same way.

days.title: Grassy saddle and the Western Dihedral
days.objective: Climb the Western Dihedral and return to the car
days.note: climberkyle reports exactly 2 hours from the car to the grassy saddle via the ford and the steep, dirty gullies; the row allows about 3 hours. From the saddle, go left to the base of Skeena26, scramble about 100 m of class 4 ramps, and cross the gully to the far western wall, about 1 more hour. The route follows a large reddish right-facing corner with 4-inch-plus cracks. A rack to 4 inches and two 60 m ropes are the usual recommendation. Gain is from the row; miles and hours are estimates.

notes: OpenBeta confirms only the 5.8 grade and the 2017 first ascent (Enger, Lewis, Daubert); its description is empty. No opened source documents the descent; rappelling the route with the recommended two ropes is likely but unconfirmed. No source gives the distance, so 5.0 mi round trip is an estimate. The row's 2,200 ft is consistent with the 1,376 ft trailhead to the 3,249 ft saddle plus the scramble and route.

itinerary.cal: July through September, once the slopes to Sawtooth Pass are mostly melted out. An Olympic National Park wilderness permit is required for the Flapjack Lakes camp. Most parties take 2 days, with the Fin climbed on the way out.
itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day Olympics plan: hike about 7.7 mi to Flapjack Lakes, then climb to Sawtooth Pass for the Fin's short 5.4 chimney route before hiking out to Staircase.

days.title: Staircase to Flapjack Lakes
days.note: Follow the North Fork Skokomish trail about 3.4-3.7 mi to the junction, then 3.6 mi up the right fork to Flapjack Lakes. WTA gives about 15.4 mi round trip and 3,050 ft. The camps are established sites with a bear wire and toilets.

days.title: Climb the Fin and hike out
days.objective: Summit the Fin and return to Staircase
days.note: Head toward Gladys Divide and leave the trail near 4,400 ft before the small pond. Climb the open snow and rock slope southeast to the narrow chute of Sawtooth Pass, then follow the ridge east to the route, which Mountain Project describes as steep pillow basalt with a classic chimney. Reverse with a short rappel or downclimb to the pass, then hike out. Gain and loss are derived from the row's 5,500 ft high point and the 3,850 ft lakes; the side-trip miles are a row-based estimate.

notes: The row's 13.7 km one-way (about 8.5 mi, about 17 mi round trip) and 5,500 ft gain agree with WTA's 7.7 mi one-way to the lakes plus the side trip to Sawtooth Pass. Mountain Project lists the route as 5.4. Hours for day 2 are an estimate. The descent is noted in the row as not consistently documented.

reason: Row has no grade, elevations, approach or waypoints, and the peak (one of several 'South Peak's) cannot be identified with confidence; no route-specific source found.
Row is empty (no grade, approach, elevations) and no route-specific source was found for this South Peak face.
Row has only a Class 4 grade; no approach, elevations or waypoints, and no opened source documents this route.
Row is empty and no route-specific source was found.
Row has only a Class 4 grade and no approach or elevations; no route-specific source found.

Remote Gunsight Range objective via the Downey/Bachelor Creek approach and glacier travel; no trip report or route page for South Peak's West Face could be opened, so day counts and timing would be invented.
No waypoints or elevations in the row and no opened source describes the Haunted Wall or its multi-day Easy Ridge/Challenger approach timing.
Obscure first-ascent-style route (Park Creek approach, rappel onto glacier, bivy at rib base); no opened source gives timing or camps beyond the row, so an honest day plan is not possible.

Only one source found (Steph Abegg Southern Pickets 1, which used the NE Ridge for rappels, not as an ascent route); no second independent source reachable (SummitPost/Mountaineers/CascadeClimbers 403).

Only one opened source (Steph Abegg Southern Pickets 1: Goodell Creek trailhead to Terror Basin about 7 hr, Barrier crossing to a Chopping Block ridge camp at 6,400 ft, single-rope rappels down the NE Ridge). A second independent source could not be reached, so the plan is held back.
Row has no approach, elevations or waypoints; the only Pyramid source found (Steph Abegg) covers the West Ridge, not the East Ridge.
Only approach information was found (WTA Trap Lake: 11 mi round trip, 2,700 ft). No opened source describes the North Face climb, its timing, or the high point gain from camp.

Only the WTA Royal Basin hike page (16 mi round trip, 2,650 ft to Upper Royal Basin) could be opened. The CascadeClimbers and Mountaineers pages on the Incisor returned 403, so the climb portion has no source.

Only a thin personal log (sverdina: short approach into the Whistler-Cutthroat basin, ridge from the saddle, easy SW gully descent) was readable. Mountaineers and SummitPost returned 403, and there is no distance, gain or timing to build from.
Row is completely empty (no grade, approach, elevations) and no source was found.
